title: Reeve Aleutian Airways 8
summary: During cruise climb from Cold Bay to Seattle, the No. 4 propeller separated from the Lockheed L-188C Electra, struck the fuselage creating an eight-foot gash, depressurizing the cabin and jamming flight and engine controls. The crew diverted to Anchorage using unconventional control methods including autopilot and landing gear manipulation. All 15 occupants survived.
probable_cause: The propeller on engine No. 4 separated in flight. The exact cause of the propeller separation was not determined since the propeller fell in the ocean during the occurrence.

factors.evidence: The No. 4 propeller separated from the aircraft and struck the fuselage, creating an eight-foot gash in the lower fuselage (p. 1)
The propeller strike resulted in decompression of the cabin (p. 1)
The flight controls became jammed and the engines would not respond to throttle movement (p. 1)
The crew were only able to climb and descend by retracting and extending the landing gear with the No. 2 engine shut down (p. 1)
The aircraft was landed safely at Anchorage with no injuries to the 15 occupants despite severe damage (p. 1)

events.text: Aircraft departed Cold Bay Airport for Seattle, Washington
Aircraft climbed through FL190 toward FL250, indicating cruise climb phase
Aircrew noted unusual vibration; attempts to isolate the vibration were unsuccessful
Flight engineer went aft to observe the engines and propellers but noted nothing unusual
Flight attendant went forward to advise captain that nothing was observed
No. 4 propeller separated from the aircraft and struck the fuselage, causing major damage to the lower fuselage
Cabin depressurized and flight controls became jammed; engines would not respond to throttle movement
Crew diverted to Anchorage International Airport and used autopilot for minimal control
Crew climbed and descended by retracting and extending the landing gear with No. 2 engine shut down to manipulate aircraft attitude
Aircraft landed safely at Anchorage International Airport; veered off runway into a ditch but all occupants survived
Engines were shut down to decelerate the aircraft

notes: Report is brief (5 pages) with limited specific timing information
Event times t are estimated from departure (1324 AKD) and accident time (1355 AKD)
Exact cause of propeller separation not determined per report
No formal safety recommendations found in report
All events extracted from Analysis section (p. 1) and Findings section (p. 2)
